title: Early joints and late joints on the south side
summary: They compare early and late audiences and moonlighting musicians like Jimmie Noone and Oliver.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: I wonder if you recognize that same thing on the south side. There were, uh, early joints till 12 or 1 and there were late joints till morning. Did you happen to remember that?
And, uh, I, I wonder if it wasn't, uh, for the, the, uh, same two audiences. The dancing audience and the listening audience.
That may very well have been. I hadn't thought of that. The Deleuze used to stay on till 10.

Of course, there may have been such things as swing shift business. I don't know. But, uh, half a dozen of the fellows on the south side were moonlighters working two jobs. Jimmy Noon was one. He worked over here at the ballroom, uh, on the west side, uh, Dreamland ballroom. And then would go down to the Apex Club for a couple of hours. And, uh, Oliver had, on many occasions, had two jobs. Darnell talks about the theater jobs and then the late jobs. Well, these late jobs, uh, may have been, um, late shows, uh, such as Grand Terrace or something of that sort. So that, uh, slightly different. But, uh. The Sunset was a late one. I remember that. Uh, I wonder if they were appealing to the after theater and the musician and the, uh, uh, well, the night people.
